question: The Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur iron ore belt lies in which of the following groups of states?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh - Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt is one of the major iron ore belts in India.
 
• This belt primarily spans across the states of Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra.
 
• It is known for having rich deposits of high-grade hematite iron ore.
 
• Prominent mines in this region include Bailadila in Chhattisgarh and the mines in the Chandrapur district of Maharashtra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hematite Iron Ore**:

 
 
• Hematite ore is the most important industrial iron ore in terms of the quantity used.
 
• It has a high iron content, typically around 70% iron.
 
• This ore is primarily used in the production of steel.
 
 
 
• **Iron Ore Mining in India**:
 
 
• India is one of the leading producers of iron ore in the world.
 
• The major iron ore belts in India are Odisha-Jharkhand, Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur, Bellary-Chitradurga-Chikmagalur-Tumkur in Karnataka, and Maharashtra-Goa.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance**:
 
 
• Iron ore mining contributes significantly to the economy, especially in terms of exports and employment generation.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the industrial development of a country.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**:
 
 
• Iron ore mining can have significant environmental impacts, including deforestation, soil erosion, and pollution.
 
• Efforts are made to mitigate these impacts through sustainable mining practices and rehabilitation of mined areas.
